basis: Lymphocyte proliferation defines the disorder; the supplied hierarchy identifies an inborn error of immunity. No additional organ is shared across the umbrella.
Cutaneous and oral/GI blistering with scarring; contractures and mitten deformities in 80-99%. Anemia is secondary to losses/inflammation; visual loss occurs in <30%.
Defining Meckel triad: cystic renal dysplasia, encephalocele and polydactyly. Hepatic fibrosis and pulmonary hypoplasia each occur in 1/4 reported patients.
Hyperostotic skeletal dysplasia with muscle atrophy and joint limitation. Hearing impairment, optic injury and neuropathy are each occasional (<30%).
Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability defines neurodevelopmental dysfunction; no additional organ damage is established.
Growth hormone-secreting anterior pituitary adenoma. Acromegaly and gigantism are separately diagnosed hormonal syndromes.
Localized destruction and atrophy of brain parenchyma; the underlying vascular or inflammatory cause is not inherent to every case.
Benign neoplasm arising in or occupying the cerebellum.
The definition identifies neurodevelopmental dysfunction, ophthalmologic disease including myopia, and orthopedic abnormalities as characteristic components.
Primary microcephaly with brain malformations; adducted thumbs 11/12 and contractures 1/2; glaucoma/ptosis 1/2. Small ocular sample; pigment macules do not establish skin injury.
Immune-mediated demyelination of peripheral nerves and roots. Weakness and impaired swallowing reflect nerve dysfunction, without separate muscle or GI injury.
Inflamed benign epidermal keratosis; local inflammation does not establish an autoimmune or infectious mechanism.
Drug-resistant mycobacterial infection; pulmonary disease directly damages lung tissue in most patients, approximately 80% or more. Other sites are not consistently affected.
Poliovirus infection destroys spinal motor neurons. Paralysis and subsequent muscle wasting arise from denervation rather than primary muscle infection.
Infection produces bullous injury of the tympanic membrane.
Gamma-sarcoglycanopathy causes skeletal muscular dystrophy. Cardiac involvement varies across cohorts and is not securely established at >=30%; no primary nerve disease.
Tumor originates in vaginal smooth muscle, a reproductive site outside the axes. Smooth muscle histology does not make this a locomotor-system tumor.
Nonsyndromic inherited hearing loss with cochlear malformation and enlarged vestibular aqueduct.
Fungal infection causes corneal ulceration and tissue damage.
Lymphoid malignancy qualifies for both blood-cell and lymphoma mechanism axes. The organ of origin varies across subtypes; none is shared across the umbrella.
Coagulation disorder causing hypercoagulability. Vascular thromboses are separately diagnosed events rather than intrinsic vascular damage shared across thrombophilias.
Arylsulfatase A deficiency causes central and peripheral demyelination; optic atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Incontinence is neurologic; gallbladder and hearing disease occur in <30%.
Iron metabolism disorder; hepatic fibrosis in 80-99%, cardiomyopathy and arthropathy in 30-79%. Endocrine injury shares the primary axis; pigmentation alone is not skin damage.
Clonal marrow disorder defined by excess myeloblasts and ineffective hematopoiesis. Progression to acute leukemia is a later risk.
Keratinization disease with inherited platelet production defects in the supplied hierarchy; the definition establishes an enzymatic defect of sphingolipid metabolism.
